title.narrative: Countering Illicit Trafficking and Transnational Organized Crime in Africa (CITOC)

description.narrative: The Action aims to strengthen Africa's resilience to transnational security threats by enhancing the capacities of African countries to prevent, protect against, and combat illicit trafficking and transnational organised crime (TOC). It is structured around a main component focused on combating illicit trafficking along major trade and transport land corridors, supported by two additional components that specifically address the trafficking in substandard and falsified medical products and cybercrime respectively. Primarily focused on West African countries, the Action¿s scope extends to several countries in Central, East and Southern Africa. By concentrating on critical socio-economic sectors ¿ transport, health, and digital-related ¿ that show particular vulnerability to organised crime, it contributes to the 360-degree approach of the EU Global Gateway Strategy and advances EU-Africa partnership¿s goals of peace, security, and prosperity.The Specific Objectives [components] of this Action are to:1.Contribute to the reduction of illicit trade and other forms of organised crime and trafficking along major trade and transport land corridors in West Africa costal countries and Cameroon.2. Strengthen the capacity to prevent, detect and respond to the trafficking of medical products across West, East and Southern Africa countries, with a focus on Substandard and Falsified Medical Products (SFMP).3.Enhance the capacity to effectively tackle online fraud and cybercrime in West and Central Africa.Component 1: Trafficking corridors. Major trade and transport corridors often intersect with trafficking routes and hubs. New investments improving connectedness of markets and territories are likely to exacerbate opportunities for criminal exploitation. These risks are especially acute in environments where governance and regulatory capacities are weak. In West Africa, road networks also play a critical role in the operations of armed groups, serving as both a revenue source and a means to exert control over local populations. To address these challenges, the Action will strengthen the capabilities of frontline actors in countering illicit trafficking along the established Global Gateway Trade and Transport Corridors through a mix of local and cross-border activities across coastal West African countries and Cameroon. It will enhance law enforcement capabilities through innovative, locally-designed pilot initiatives; encourage harmonised regional control measures and cross-border cooperation through joint operations and intelligence sharing. The focus will be on land corridors, which are often under-prioritized compared to air and maritime routes, despite accounting for 80% of goods transport and 90% of people movement on the continent.Component 2: Trafficking in Substandard and Falsified Medical Products (SFMP). In Sub-Saharan Africa, SFMP account for 30% of medical products in circulation, and up to 55% in West Africa, leading to thousands of deaths annually. The illicit trafficking of pharmaceuticals is not only deadly and lucrative (estimated 10 to 25 times more profitable than drug trafficking) but also serves as a privileged avenue for laundering illicit proceeds and funding illegal activities. Joining EU efforts to combat the trafficking of pharmaceutical and medical products will contribute to both public health and security outcomes, while supporting the EU Global Gateway Health Strategy and complementing the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) on manufacturing and access to vaccines, medicines, and health technologies in Africa (MAV+) efforts.
